title: Issue One
summary: Issue One covers Western New York investment and industry news from Sept. 28 to Oct. 9, 2026. Solstice Advanced Materials announced a $49M Buffalo R&D expansion and Goodyear said it will close its Niagara Falls chemical plant, while defense contracts touched Liverpool, Syracuse and Niagara Falls.

items.headline: Solstice to invest $49M expanding Buffalo R&D center
items.note: Solstice will invest $49M to expand its Buffalo R&D center, adding 12 jobs, with up to $1.4M in state Excelsior tax credits. The governor's and company's announcements quote different spokespeople and name forms.

items.headline: Goodyear to close Niagara Falls chemical plant
items.note: Goodyear plans to close its Niagara Falls chemical plant, with production expected to end Oct. 31, 2026. Sources differ on jobs: about 85 across two sites (SEC filing) vs. 60 local (Niagara Gazette).

items.headline: Lockheed Martin's Liverpool radar work gets $18.9M contract change
items.note: An $18.9M change to an existing Air Force radar contract with work in Liverpool. The ~$1B figure is the contract ceiling, not new spending.

items.headline: $11.2M radar-parts contract splits work between Liverpool and Lithuania
items.note: An $11.2M radar-parts contract change with work in Liverpool and Lithuania; the Liverpool share is not disclosed.

items.headline: Niagara Air Reserve Station awards base-support contract
items.note: Base maintenance and logistics contract at Niagara Air Reserve Station: $38.8M ceiling, $14,317 obligated so far. Contractor identity is still being confirmed.

items.headline: SRC reports $37M Air Force prototype award
items.note: SRC reports a $37M Air Force prototype award for its Ghost Mantis technology. No production commitment or local job count disclosed.

items.headline: Gekko Photonics confirms Rochester office, plans local hiring
items.note: Gekko Photonics says it has a Rochester office and plans local engineering hires and regional suppliers; no headcount or facility announced yet.
